content.value_statement: Frontend teams need consistent CSS without ad hoc overrides. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward Tailwind utilities and design tokens.
actual_capabilities: Guides CSS and Tailwind utility work in React components.
Encourages use of design system colors, spacing, and typography.
Helps decide between Tailwind utilities and custom CSS.
Supports Tailwind theme extension work with the `@theme` directive.
Emphasizes CSS bundle optimization through purging and tree-shaking.
limitations: Does not include the full referenced frontend CSS standards inside the skill.
Does not run CSS linters, formatters, or build tools by itself.
Does not define project-specific token values or component APIs.
Relies on project context to apply styling guidance correctly.

use_cases.title: Standardize Component Styling
use_cases.description: Apply Tailwind utility classes consistently while editing React components.

use_cases.title: Protect Design System Tokens
use_cases.description: Keep colors, spacing, and typography aligned with an existing design system.

use_cases.title: Review CSS Changes
use_cases.description: Check new styling work for unnecessary custom CSS and production CSS concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one frontend component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-css skill to review this component's styling for Tailwind consistency, token usage, and unnecessary custom CSS.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Custom CSS
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert isolated custom styles to framework utilities
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-css skill to replace avoidable custom CSS with Tailwind utilities while preserving the current visual behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Extend Theme Tokens
prompt_templates.scenario: Add or review Tailwind theme values
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-css skill to assess whether these theme extensions belong in the design system and how they should be named.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Styling Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across components and CSS files
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-css skill to audit this styling approach for utility-first consistency, responsive patterns, bundle size, and long-term maintainability.

output_examples.input: Review a React button for Tailwind consistency.
output_examples.output: The review flags duplicated spacing choices, recommends token-based colors, and explains when a small custom class is justified.
The response checks whether the new values match design system patterns and suggests clearer token names.

output_examples.input: Audit a CSS update before release.
output_examples.output: The audit highlights responsive gaps, unnecessary overrides, and bundle-size concerns from unused or duplicated styles.

best_practices: Prefer design tokens and existing Tailwind utilities before adding CSS.
Keep custom CSS small, named clearly, and tied to reusable patterns.
Use Tailwind breakpoints consistently for responsive behavior.
anti_patterns: Adding one-off CSS for styles already covered by utilities.
Overriding framework styles globally without a documented reason.
Introducing new colors, spacing, or typography outside the design system.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents write and review frontend CSS using Tailwind utilities and design system tokens.

faq.question: Does it generate complete visual designs?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on CSS implementation choices, consistency, and maintainability.

faq.question: Can it work with React components?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explicitly covers Tailwind classes in .tsx and .jsx components.

faq.question: Does it replace a CSS linter?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, but it does not execute linting or build commands.

faq.question: What CSS methodology does it favor?
faq.answer: It favors Tailwind utility classes, minimal custom CSS, and design system alignment.

faq.question: Is the skill self-contained?
faq.answer: Not fully. It currently references a frontend CSS standards file outside the skill directory.
